issue_semantics: Forecasts use the latest-revised values the fixed lag rule expects to be published as of the retrieval date; issue month is the latest month for which that rule yields a complete feature set. Individual release dates are not audited per origin (spot-checked against the BLS calendar at build time). Backtest origins simulate the same rule at past month-ends.

evaluation.design: Expanding-window rolling-origin backtest; direct model per horizon.
caveats: Latest-revised data, not historical vintages: BLS revises these series (annual JOLTS/CES benchmarking). Backtest accuracy approximates and usually flatters real-time performance.

Fixed publication lags (JOLTS 2 months, others 1) approximate the release calendar; actual release dates vary. Claims are weekly; a calendar month of claims is not fully published until days after it ends.
Claims (ICSA) are seasonally adjusted weekly counts averaged into calendar months; the week-to-month mapping is approximate.

Prequential evaluation, not a fixed-model test: every prediction, including 2026 test months, comes from a model refit on everything published by that origin. 'Untouched 2026' means 2026 played no role in model selection or interval calibration only.
Roughly 24 selection and up to 9 final-test origins per horizon: per-year scores have wide sampling error.
Elevated-alert evaluation is exploratory and historical only, not calibrated to a required false-positive rate; no zero-false-positive guarantee is possible or made. It is not a risk recommendation.

Intervals are residual bands calibrated on 2024-2025 selection origins of the published model. Selection-era coverage is in-calibration (optimistic); 2026 coverage is held out. Where held-out coverage falls well short of the nominal 80%, the band ran too narrow and is labeled so.

huber_targetonly is an exploratory ablation using only lagged target values on identical folds. Full-model improvements over it on the 2024-2025 selection era and on 2026 are reported descriptively; with ~24 selection and ~9 test origins, the incremental value of the economic predictors carries wide uncertainty, and no causal feature importance is claimed.
Leakage tests validate the cutoff logic on the latest data snapshot only; they cannot prove what was actually available historically - the vintage caveat stands.
Forecasts describe this JOLTS measure only. They are not causal claims about the economy and not WARN notice predictions.
Source gaps handled by past-only carry-forward with a missingness indicator (never the target, never reaching forward): UNRATE ['2025-10']

UNRATE.2025-10: Never published: the 2025 federal government shutdown halted CPS collection and BLS cancelled the October 2025 household report.
